summary: This benchmark evaluates the portability of a distilled 261k-parameter memory module into an independently initialized 14.3M-parameter recipient model using causal interchange interventions. The methodology is well-controlled with matched counterfactual swap sites, paired confidence intervals, and explicit negative controls. While the evaluation is conducted on a synthetic register-routing benchmark without a directly provided repository artifact in the submission metadata, the experimental reporting is thorough and statistically sound.
strengths: Methodologically sound use of causal interchange interventions with rigorous negative controls (initialization site swap vs. later-write control site producing 0 switches).
Precise statistical reporting with prespecified noninferiority margins and 95% paired confidence intervals across 1,024 programs and 2,048 program pairs.
Comprehensive isolation of schedule sensitivity by examining event reordering while holding ground-truth answers constant.
Transparent documentation of execution environment (MLX 0.32.4 on Apple M5 Ultra) and disclosure of AI assistance.
weaknesses: The evaluation is restricted to a synthetic register-tracking task, leaving generalizability to natural language or diverse pretraining distributions unverified.
The text is extremely condensed and dense (under 650 words), omitting visual diagrams of the module interface architecture beyond external Markdown hyperlinks.
No supporting repository was directly attached via submission metadata, limiting direct in-line execution verification and requiring a text-only designation.
suggestions: Extend the interchange intervention evaluation beyond synthetic register tracking to standard NLP or multi-hop reasoning tasks.
Include an architectural schematic illustrating the exact projection layer alignment and displacement addressing interface between donor and recipient models.
Directly bundle and release the standalone test scripts and weight checkpoints via the official repository submission field to enable verified code badge status.

claims.text: This is an interchange intervention, a method with an established causal interpretation for specified counterfactuals. [Geiger et al., 2021]
The experiments used MLX 0.32.4 on an Apple M5 Ultra.
claims.source: https://pypi.org/project/mlx/ and Apple M5 Ultra platform announcements

claims.text: Exchanging one internal value between two programs made their answers switch to each other’s correct answer in 2,018 of 2,022 initially correct pairs. Swapping a value at the later-write control site produced zero such switches.
claims.source: Internal experimental reporting in submission body backed by paired benchmark counts

novelty_vs_existing.title: Causal Abstractions of Neural Networks
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies interchange intervention techniques specifically to benchmark cross-recipient portability of a distilled memory submodule rather than purely analyzing static causal abstraction within a single network.
